title: Admin Quickfix Gallery and Playwright Runbook Trigger Integration
creator: Priya Nambiar
description: Build a curated Admin Quickfix Gallery: a first-class Console surface where on-call and SREs can discover vetted, parameterized 'quickfix' runbook tasks, preview a dry-run, and execute in a sandboxed environment. Integrate a Playwright-based runner to trigger safe, observable UI-driven operations for workflows that require browser-backed steps (e.g., web console toggles, support portal interactions). The feature reduces toil for common incident remediation, centralizes change history, and ensures safety via RBAC, dry-run, limits, and multi-step approvals.
acceptance_criteria: Console UI exposes a Quickfix Gallery with category filters, search, and per-task metadata (owner, last-run, tags)
Each quickfix maps to a runbook-as-task manifest (id, params schema, required_role, timeout, dry_run_command)
Playwright runner executes browser-backed steps in an isolated container with recording of stdout/stderr and artifacts (HAR/screenshots) stored to S3-compatible object store
Dry-run mode validates input and shows a simulated plan without making changes and must be available before a real run
Audit log entries (user, task id, params, result, duration) are written to the central audit pipeline and visible in Console activity view
RBAC enforcement: only users with role 'ops_executor' or higher can run non-dry quickfixes; parameterized tasks enforce must-approve flags for dangerous ops
Automated tests for two representative quickfixes (restart-service, rotate-cache-key) run in CI with Playwright smoke test coverage
Metrics emitted: run_duration_ms, success_count, failure_count, dry_run_count, artifact_size_bytes, and per-task latency p95, available in Console telemetry
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Schema and Backend - define quickfix manifest spec, storage table, and runner API (week 1)
Phase 2: Playwright Runner - containerized runner image, secrets injection path, HAR/screenshot capture, sandbox limits (week 2)
Phase 3: Console UI - gallery list, task detail page, dry-run UX, approval flow UI (week 3)
Phase 4: RBAC and Audit - integrate with account RBAC, write audit events to event pipeline, and hook Console activity view (week 3)
Phase 5: CI and Canary - add unit/integration tests, deploy to staging, and run canary with 'site reliability' team (week 4)
Phase 6: Rollout - soft launch to internal SRE and support, collect feedback, iterate, then enable company-wide (week 5)
rollout_plan: Internal-only beta behind feature flag for SRE and oncall@redwood (day 0)
Feedback window: 2 weeks. Surface issues as follow-ups (performance, UX, missing tasks)
Enable dry-run-only for all users for one week after beta to let teams validate behavior
Enable execution for ops_executor role after successful canary and security signoff
Add incremental Quickfixes by subject-matter owners; require PR with manifest + tests to add to Gallery
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Playwright runners could be abused to exfiltrate secrets - Mitigation: runner runs in short-lived ephemeral containers with no host network by default, secrets injected via one-time tokens, and strict outbound egress policy
Risk: A misconfigured quickfix performs unsafe actions - Mitigation: require manifest 'dangerous' flag, manual approval step for dangerous tasks, and gating by role
Risk: High load on runner infra during incidents - Mitigation: rate-limits per-team, circuit breaker on failures, and fallback to human-run KB articles
Risk: Audit logs missing critical fields - Mitigation: enforce schema in API, schema validation tests in CI, and end-to-end test to assert audit events arrive in pipeline
telemetry: Emit run.requested and run.completed events to telemetry pipeline with properties: task_id, user_id, params_hash, result_status
Record runner.container_start and runner.container_end spans for tracing and link to request id
Expose Console dashboard tiles for per-task success rate and p95 latency
Send alert when quickfix failure_rate > 5% for a given task over 30m rolling window
